title: Between Dawn and Evening
relation: A difference in how guidance is offered
summary: Solarius and Vesper ask how a warning can protect without pretending to know every road. Their conversation is optional and changes neither independent story.

aa: Judgment and Shelter meet at an open door. Solarius will name a danger; Vesper will keep a place to recover. Neither calls a warning permission to own the traveler.
ab: Judgment and Testimony compare the limits of their evidence. Solarius accepts that a clear verdict must not invent a missing witness; Vesper leaves the unknown road unfilled.
ba: Sanctuary and Shelter offer two welcomes without making either exclusive. Bread and light sustain the traveler, but neither host demands allegiance as payment.
bb: Sanctuary and Testimony refuse a comforting falsehood. Solarius offers care before agreement, while Vesper records uncertainty without using it as a reason to withhold help.
